Orders: PED-1011 amount 20.00, expires at 10:00 -03:00. PED-1012 same.

Statement: one line, e2e_id E1000000010001, type payment, amount 20.00, time 09:00 -03:00, payer, txid: PED-1011, description: "pagamento pedido PED-1012"

Link rule: link by txid when present; otherwise by order id in description. Here txid is PED-1011, so link to order PED-1011. Even though description mentions PED-1012, we ignore description because txid present.

Thus payment linked to PED-1011.

Now compute status.

Order PED-1011: payments distinct e2e ids linked: one: E1000000010001. Total amount received = 20.00.

Expires_at 10:00 -03:00. Payment time 09:00 -03:00 which is before expires_at, so on time.

Now status rules: we need to check which applies.

First check unpaid: there is payment, so not unpaid.

Then refunded: refunds? No refund lines. So not refund.

Then underpaid: received amount less than order amount? Received equal, so not underpaid.

Then overpaid: received more than order amount? No.

Then late_paid: exactly amount received, after expires_at? No, it's before.

Then paid: exactly amount received, at or before expires_at. Yes.

So status "paid".

Now order PED-1012: no linked payments. No payment lines linked. So status unpaid.

Payments list: must include distinct e2e_ids linked to order, including refund lines. For PED-1011: ["E1000000010001"]; sorted (only one). For PED-1012: no linked payments, so empty list? Probably list should be empty array.

Orphans: list distinct e2e_ids of payment lines that cannot be linked to any order. Our payment line linked to PED-1011, so no orphan. Also refund lines never orphans. So orphans empty array.

Construct JSON:

{
 "orders": {
   "PED-1011": {"status":"paid","payments":["E1000000010001"]},
   "PED-1012": {"status":"unpaid","payments":[]}
 },
 "orphans": []
}

Make sure ordering of keys correct: "orders" then "orphans". Within orders, order ids maybe any order but keep as given.

Return as JSON code block.
